passages.note: House Third Reading: Diaz voted Yea on this single-subject empowerment-scholarship bill, 31-26-3-0-0.
Diaz is listed as a co-sponsor of HB2853 as filed; the Governor signed the bill as Chapter 388.

passages.provision_quote: Notwithstanding section 15-2401, beginning in the 2022-2023 school year, in this chapter, unless the context otherwise requires, "qualified student" includes a resident of this state who both: 1. Is eligible to enroll in a public school in this state in any of the following: ( a ) A preschool program for children with disabilities. ( b ) A kindergarten program. ( c ) Any of grades one through twelve. 2. Does not otherwise qualify for an Arizona empowerment scholarship account pursuant to this chapter.
passages.note: New section 15-2401.01 makes any public-school-eligible resident a qualified student, the annex's own description of a universal instrument.

rows.reasoning: Diaz co-sponsored and voted Yea (House Third Reading, 31-26-3-0-0) on HB2853 (2022), a single-subject Arizona empowerment scholarship accounts bill. Its new section 15-2401.01 makes any resident eligible to enroll in public school (preschool for disabilities, kindergarten, or grades one through twelve) a qualified student without otherwise qualifying, and the Act's 'qualified school' definition is not limited to nonreligious schools, matching rung 5's text that 'education funding follows the student to any school — public, private, or religious — chosen by the family.'
